source.title: Safety of Antiseizure Medications During Direct Oral Anticoagulant Therapy in Epilepsy
source.source_type: original investigation; retrospective cohort target-trial emulation
source.access_scope: public structured abstract only; article body, figures, tables, supplements, and bibliography unavailable without authenticated/purchased access in this run

extraction_metadata.external_verification: JAMA Neurology public article page checked 2026-08-23 for current abstract and access status.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study compared thromboembolic events, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality across commonly used antiseizure medications in adults with epilepsy receiving direct oral anticoagulants.

The investigators used a retrospective cohort design that emulated a target trial for each antiseizure medication group against an active comparator, with 1:1 propensity score matching in four cohorts to estimate a sustained-monotherapy per-protocol outcome.
Participant data came from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, a federated deidentified electronic health record network spanning 165 health care organizations internationally.

Adults aged 18 years or older with epilepsy were eligible; the abstract reports exclusions for recent vitamin K antagonist use, strong non-antiseizure CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein modulators, and major vascular events in the prior year.

population.label: Adults with epilepsy receiving DOACs
exclusion_criteria: Major vascular event in the prior year

atoms.canonical_statement: Participant follow-up began at a prespecified 90-day landmark, and the reported analyses were performed from January through March 2026.
The exposure groups were levetiracetam, valproate, moderate enzyme-inducing antiseizure medications, and strong enzyme-inducing antiseizure medications, each evaluated during monotherapy.

exposures.details: Examples reported in the abstract include carbamazepine and phenytoin.

atoms.canonical_statement: Lamotrigine or lacosamide formed one pooled active-comparator reference group.

exposures.details: Pooled active comparator group in the abstract.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary thromboembolic composite included ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and systemic or peripheral embolism.

outcome.definition: Ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, or systemic/peripheral embolism.

atoms.canonical_statement: Major bleeding was a primary outcome.
All-cause mortality was a primary outcome.

Of 2.29 million adults with epilepsy, 40,932 were DOAC eligible, 26,962 had DOAC-antiseizure medication overlap within 6 months, 10,209 were monotherapy eligible, and 9,529 initiators formed the analytic cohort.

population.label: Analytic cohort after reported screening and monotherapy eligibility flow

atoms.canonical_statement: The analytic cohort contained 9,529 initiators with mean age 63 years (SD 18); 4,869 participants (51%) were female.
Levetiracetam initiators numbered 5,473 participants (57% of the analytic cohort).
Strong enzyme-inducing ASM initiators numbered 1,395 participants (15% of the analytic cohort).
Valproate initiators numbered 1,006 participants (11% of the analytic cohort).
Moderate enzyme-inducing ASM initiators numbered 382 participants (4% of the analytic cohort).
Compared with lamotrigine/lacosamide, levetiracetam was associated with higher thromboembolic risk (HR 1.98, 95% CI 1.37 to 2.87).

population.label: Matched adults with epilepsy receiving DOACs

exposures.details: Pooled active comparator group in the abstract.

atoms.canonical_statement: Compared with lamotrigine/lacosamide, levetiracetam was associated with higher all-cause mortality (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.23 to 2.08).

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that antiseizure medication selection was associated with distinct thromboembolic, bleeding, and mortality risks in adults with epilepsy receiving DOACs and may represent a modifiable contributor to clinical outcomes.
